bizStartsToMargin.doc: Lab round 3 (G10, needs sign-off): builders start a Shops, Leisure, Industry, Offices or Farms tile only while that sector's supply-line margin m̄′ (§5.12, A6: the pipeline's cost included) is at least the normal margin. By the bare §5.2 rule the lagged meter D kept lots growing for months after the margin had turned (Leisure 59 → 209 jobs in a year, then closures back to 26), a boom-and-bust that crossed zero 6–8 times in 20 days. false gives the bare rule.

homesStartsToGap.doc: Lab round 3 (G10, needs sign-off): builders start a Homes tile only while that tier's built and building homes fall short of its demand at the Homes meter's vacancy target, less a develop.homesQueue share kept waiting (§5.2, the supply line of §5.8). By the bare §5.2 rule z = D + L keeps high-L lots growing into a glut (D at −20 only halves the growth chance), so £ vacancy overshot to 8–11% after each bot zoning wave and the £ Homes meter swung ±20 on a ~40-month cycle. false gives the bare rule.

emptyHomesFloor.doc: Lab round 2, the mirror of A9 (needs sign-off): a Homes tier with no homes built or building cannot be over-supplied, so its meter's vacancy side is floored at 0, and with no residents of its own the needs penalty (A10) does not apply: only waiting demand moves it. By the bare §5.8 ratio an empty tier reads 0/5 = 0, a target of -100, and sat pinned there for 190+ months in towns with nothing for the well-off (G10, the 20.1 'stuck unactionable meter' probe). false gives the bare formula.

tickMs.doc: Real milliseconds per game week (one tick).

sprintTicks.doc: Founding Fortnight length: ticks run on demand by the sprint move (§2.3).

sprintMinGapMs.doc: Minimum real time between two tapped sprint ticks.

sprintAutoMs.doc: "Play it all": one sprint tick every this many ms.

regionalHour.doc: Default Regional Day hour, Europe/London local time.

devRegionalTicks.doc: Dev clock only: a Regional Day every this many ticks (§2.6).

napAfterMs.doc: A county naps this long after the last hello (A21: 72 h).

heartbeatMs.doc: A paused or napping county writes a heartbeat this often.

awayAfterMs.doc: A town is Away after this long without a hello (§2.4: 48 h).

meters.doc: Starting meters in METER order: Homes £/££/£££, Shops, Leisure, Industry, Offices, Farms (A11).

margin.doc: Starting smoothed sector margins m̄ and m̄′ (A11).

price.doc: Starting county goods and food price index (A11).

rating.doc: Starting rating as an index into RATINGS (AAA=0 … B=5): A (A11).

surveyFee.doc: Parcel survey fee per tier number (§3.1).

zonePerTile.doc: Zoning cost per tile; free in v1 (§9.3 lists none).

hillRoadMult.doc: Road build cost multiplier on Hills sites, on slope tiles (§3.1).

forestBuildMult.doc: Building cost multiplier on Forest sites (timber, §3.1).

riverWaterMult.doc: Water facility cost multiplier on River sites (§3.1).

sameDayRefund.doc: Refund share when bulldozing a civic building or road built since the last Regional Day (§9.3).

civicTicks.doc: Civic construction ticks by footprint area: 1 tile, ≤ 4, ≤ 9, larger.

maxOps.doc: Most operations in one atomic build plan (§10.6).

undoMax.doc: Most undoable plans kept per town per day (§10.2).

pGrow.doc: Peak growth chance of a visited empty zoned tile (§5.2).

pLevel.doc: Peak level-up chance of a visited built tile (§5.2).

zMid.doc: z at which growth is half its peak.

zScale.doc: Slope of the growth logistic (Lab sweep /10 to /25).

pDecline.doc: Peak decline chance of a visited built tile.

noRoadDecline.doc: Decline chance of a built tile with no road within 2.

roadReach.doc: A zoned tile needs a road within this many tiles (§3.4).

unpoweredPenalty.doc: z penalty for an unpowered tile of level ≥ 2.

dryPenalty.doc: z penalty for an unwatered tile of level ≥ 2.

forcedDeclineOccupancy.doc: Below this occupancy for forcedDeclineMonths, a tile declines.

forcedDeclineMonths.doc: Months of low occupancy before a forced decline.

missingServiceMonths.doc: Months without road, power or water before a forced decline.

buildersBase.doc: Builders = base + Pop/per construction starts a month (§5.2; spec 6, Lab round 1: 12, so a founding hamlet builds its jobs as fast as its carts fill homes).

buildersPer.doc: Population per extra monthly construction start.

lvReq.doc: Land value needed for levels L1–L5 (§3.3).

homesTierLv.doc: LV − 0.5·Pollution needed for ££ and £££ Homes at growth (§5.2).

hotelVisitorAccess.doc: A Leisure tile grows as a hotel above this Visitor access when beds are short.

strideMul.doc: Development stride multiplier, perm(i) = (i·mul + seed) mod 4096 (A24). Odd, so a bijection.

incidentBase.doc: Monthly incident chance at zero fire coverage, risk 1 (§5.2).

incidentRisk.doc: Incident risk by ZONE order (Homes, Shops, Leisure, Industry, Offices, Farms) then civic.

incidentCap.doc: At most this share of buildings have an incident a month.

incidentTicks.doc: An incident closes a building this long.

repairShare.doc: A civic building's repair costs this share of its build cost (§5.2).

repairFreeFireCov.doc: Repairs are free where fire coverage is above this.

cartsPerTick.doc: Founders' carts: at most this many arrivals a tick (§5.2 step 4; spec 20, Lab round 1: 10, so the founders arrive no faster than work does and the hamlet's approval holds 50 by day 1).

cartsUnderPop.doc: Founders' carts run while the town is under this population.

cartsDays.doc: Founders' carts stop after this many days (A12).

lHomes.doc: Homes L = a·(LV − b) + c·(Safety − d) + e·((School + Nature)/2 − f) − g·max(0, Poll − h) − i·max(0, Noise − j) (§5.2).

lShops.doc: Shops L = a·(CustAccess − b) + c·(LV − d) − e·max(0, Crime − f) (§5.2).

lLeisure.doc: Leisure L = a·(VisitorAccess − b) + c·(LV − d) + e·(Fun + Culture − f) − g·max(0, Crime − h) (§5.2).

lIndustry.doc: Industry L = a·(Freight − b) + c·(d − LV): cheap land near the freight edge (§5.2).

lOffices.doc: Offices L = a·(LV − b) + c·(Transit − d) + e·(Culture − f) (§5.2).

farmL.doc: Farms L at Hamlet and Village, then from Town (§5.2).

farmSoil.doc: Farms L bonus on a Flatland site or river soil (§5.2).

homesPollutionBlock.doc: Cell pollution above which Homes neither grow nor level up (§5.2).

closeMonths.doc: Months a sector's smoothed margin stays below firms.closeMargin before its worst-located tiles close (§5.12).

homesQueue.doc: With rules.homesStartsToGap, the share of a Homes tier's demand (residents, squeezed, waiting and aspirants) left waiting before builders start more: the waiting list is the valve (§5.8). At 0 the £ meter settles at about 0 and flickers across ±5; at 0.03 it settles a little positive (a short waiting list) and stops crossing zero.

closeQuantile.doc: A closing sector's visited tiles decline when their desirability is in this lowest share of the sector's tiles.

smokeAlarms.doc: Incident risk multiplier with the Smoke Alarms card (§6.7: risk −40%).

alpha.doc: Meter smoothing step, D ← D + α(Target − D) (spec 0.25, τ 4 months; Lab round 2: 0.125, τ 8). The meters sit near their equilibrium and flip on month-to-month noise (construction lumps, the ±15 needs steps), not on a lag cycle: α 0.5 doubled G10's sign changes, 0.125 halved them, and the Founding Fortnight still reaches Village on day 2.

homesGain.doc: Target_H = 100·T(gain·(ratio − 1)) (§5.8; spec 2.5, Lab round 1: 5: at 2.5 a town turning away hundreds of newcomers a day read about +15, below the wants line).

vacancyTarget.doc: The Homes meter aims at this vacancy.

homesSlackTicks.doc: Review amendment to §5.8's '+5': the Homes ratio's denominator is at least this many ticks of the builders' starts (Builders/4 L1 tiles of 8 persons a tick), so an empty or tiny tier needs a build's worth of waiting demand before its meter swings; with the bare +5, 5 waiting gave 0 and 8 gave +99 (G10's pinned, sign-flipping ££ meter). A tier larger than that is unchanged. 0 gives the bare formula. Quick Lab A/B: 1 left G10's short-cycle share at 0.11, 1.5 brought it to 0.097 and kept every other passing check (2 cost 15% of the population).

needPenalty.doc: Homes meter penalty per unmet need item (A10).

needFloor.doc: The needs penalty is floored at −this.

unreachableCap.doc: A meter no zoned tile could serve is capped here (A9).

bizGain.doc: Target_s = 100·T(gain·(m̄′ − m0 − …)) (spec 4; Lab round 2: 2). At 4 a 1% swing in a sector's margin moved its target 4 points, and shops, leisure and offices crossed zero 15–20 times in 30 days (G10); at 2 the business meters halve their sign changes and a hamlet still wants its workshop.

ucWeight.doc: Weight of unfilled job slots in the business target (A5).

emptySectorJobs.doc: An empty sector is valued as if it had this many jobs (bootstrap).

wantAt.doc: A meter above this can raise a wants bubble (§5.15).

births.doc: Births per Parent per month at neutral affordability and happiness (§4.3).

settle.doc: Workers settling down into Parents per month.

comeOfAgeMonths.doc: Children grow up after this many months (16 years).

applicantDecay.doc: Applicants give up at this rate (§4.1).

aspirantDecay.doc: Aspirants give up at this rate.

studentMonths.doc: Students graduate after this many months.

birthHappy.doc: Births ×M(Happy/60; a, b), the tier's Families' happiness (§4.3).

unhappyBirths.doc: Births ×[1] while the tier's Families are below happiness [0] (§5.15).

babyBoom.doc: Births multiplier during the Baby Boom World event (§5.16).

settleAppeal.doc: Settling down ×M(FamilyAppeal/60; a, b); FamilyAppeal is the mean of Schools, Safety and Fun (§4.3).

emptyNestMax.doc: Empty nest = coming of age × min(this, P/C) (§4.3).

mobilityVac.doc: Aspirants ×M(vac/[0]; a, b), vac the next tier's homes vacancy (§4.3).

slideAtU.doc: £££ unemployment at which the slide-down rate equals slideDown (§4.3).

graduateWellOff.doc: Graduates who become £££ Workers; the rest become ££ (§4.3).

newAdultUp.doc: Tier of a new adult: £→££ with p = [0] + [1]·EduQ_sec, ££→£££ with p = [2] + [3]·EduQ_uni (§4.4).

newAdultDown.doc: Tier of a new adult: one tier down with p = this·(1 − EduQ_pri) (§4.4).

youngMonths.doc: New adults and graduates count as young (more mobile, home-grown) this long (§4.4).

longUnemployedMonths.doc: Unemployed this long count as long-term unemployed (forced movers, §5.11).

Kout.doc: Outside World arrivals that settle elsewhere (K_out).

poolExp.doc: Outside World pool grows as (1 + ΣN/4000)^exp.

poolScale.doc: ΣN scale of the Outside World pool.

n0.doc: Base Outside World pool per cohort (£W £F £R ££W ££F ££R £££W £££F £££R).

studentPool.doc: Students pool per county university seat.

friendly.doc: Net pair flow cap per day, Friendly (§8.4).

spirited.doc: Net pair flow cap per day, Spirited.

friendly.doc: Weekly net outflow cap to players, Friendly.

spirited.doc: Weekly net outflow cap to players, Spirited.

shieldAt.doc: Community Spirit starts above this 7-day net loss.

awayLossCap.doc: Away towns lose at most this a rolling week (§2.4).

homeGrown.doc: Bonus for new adults in their home town.

distance.doc: Distance penalty per minute of travel.

advert.doc: Advert bonus for the targeted cohort.

forcedUnemployed.doc: Long-term unemployed who become forced movers per month (§5.11).

veryHappy.doc: Above happiness [0], movers ×[1] and +[2] own-town utility (word of mouth, §5.15).

graduateStay.doc: Graduates' bonus to stay while offices have vacancies (§4.3).

gate.doc: Outside World gate: County Road + rail link to Kingsport + Airfield (§5.11).

gem.doc: Hidden gem: population below [0]× the county median and Buzz above [1] (§5.11).

massOffset.doc: Square-root mass sqrt(N + this) in the Outside World split (§5.11).

familyChildren.doc: Children's share of an arriving Family from the Outside World.

weights.doc: Utility weights per COHORT row: Jobs, Homes, Tax, Schools, Health, Safety, Fun, Culture, Nature, Getting around, Buzz, Needs, Inertia, μ/month (§5.11).

W0.doc: Base wage per worker-month by tier (§5.9).

maxCommute.doc: Trips longer than this are unreachable.

supportShare.doc: Support income of the unemployed as a share of the £ wage (A1).

pensionShare.doc: Pension as a share of the £ wage.

traineeShare.doc: Share of ££/£££ slots open to trainees one tier down (A4).

traineeEffect.doc: Output and staffing effect of a trainee.

linkDecay.doc: EffJobs adds linked towns' jobs × e^(−t/this).

newcomerHeads.doc: Earners per head assumed for a tier with no residents yet (its reference income for Afford).

farmFood.doc: Food units per farm tile per month (A7).

foodUnit.doc: Value of one food unit at p_food 1.0.

foodBand.doc: Kingsport's food export and import prices per unit.

goodsPerJob.doc: Goods per filled industry job per month (×Prod; spec 3.5, Lab round 1: 3.8: at 3.5 an export job sat at the 8% normal margin, so towns off the Flatland stalled at 10–12% unemployment).

goodsUnit.doc: Value of one goods unit at price 1.0.

goodsImport.doc: Kingsport goods import price ratio i_g/£1,000.

rentPerJob.doc: Premises rent per job, SECTOR order (Farms, Industry, Shops, Leisure, Offices).

inputs.doc: Input costs as a share of sales, SECTOR order.

retailShare.doc: Household retail spend share by tier α_h.

leisureShare.doc: Household leisure spend share by tier β_h.

closeMargin.doc: A sector below this smoothed margin for 3 months closes tiles.

officeShare.doc: Offices earn this share of the other sectors' local revenue (§5.12).

l5Output.doc: Output of an L5 industry job (clean makers' sheds) × this (§5.12).

flatlandFood.doc: Farm output × this on a Flatland site (A7).

inCommuterRetail.doc: Share of in-commuters' retail spend made where they work (§5.12, §8.5).

shopFoodShare.doc: Food's share of Shops' inputs; the rest is goods (§5.12).

constructionGoods.doc: Goods used per level of construction started (§5.12).

stockMonths.doc: The town keeps this many months of local use in stock before exporting (WP2c choice: Great Work pledges and short months draw on it).

surplusTau.doc: Smoothing τ of the projected surplus WP3 allocates from (§8.5).

marginTau.doc: Smoothing τ of the sector margins m̄ and m̄′ (§5.12; spec 4, Lab round 2: 8, Lab round 3: 3). The business loop is supply → margin (this lag) → meter (α's lag) → development, so two lags in series with an integrator: at τ 8 and the meter's τ 8 it rang at 2π·√(8·8) ≈ 50 months (Shops crossing zero every 25 months, G10's worst meter). Quick Lab at 3: the Shops meter's series with more than 6 sign changes fell from 19 to 3, the short-cycle share from 0.111 to 0.083; 2 and 4 did less.

labourGate.doc: LabourGate = clamp((fillRate − [0])/[1], 0, 1): no growth if you can't staff it (§5.12).

farmersMarket.doc: Farmers' Market: Shops meter target + this (§6.7).

farmersMarketFarmJobs.doc: Farmers' Market's catch, farm jobs ×this (§6.7 'farm jobs −10%'; review amendment: it was printed on the card but never applied).

leakCap.doc: Most of residents' retail spend that may leak to linked towns' shops (§5.12).

shopAppeal.doc: Shop appeal SA = ShopJobs^[0]·(1 + [1]·Fun/100), before the sales-tax gap (§5.12).

squeezedMovers.doc: Squeezed residents who become forced movers per month.

retierP.doc: Re-tiering chance on a level-up visit (gentrification).

affordableRent.doc: Rent factor inside Keep Homes Affordable.

rentOcc.doc: Rent's occupancy multiplier M(·; a, b) (§5.8).

retier.doc: A Homes tile re-tiers up when LV − 0.5·Pollution is [0] above its tier's band and the higher tier's meter is above [1] (§5.8).

filterVacancy.doc: ££ homes filter to £ at [2] a month after ££ vacancy stays above [0] for [1] months (§5.8).

filterOld.doc: £££ homes at least [0] months old (the age plane saturates at 255) with land value below the £££ band filter to ££ at [1] a month (§5.8).

shortLets.doc: Visitors per resident above [0] turn [1] of ££ homes into short lets unless Short-let Limits is on (§5.8).

powerPerJob.doc: Power demand per Shops, Leisure or Offices job.

civicPower.doc: Power demand of a civic building by footprint: 1 tile, ≤ 4, ≤ 9, larger (§3.5 "2–10 each").

civicWater.doc: Water demand of a civic building by footprint class, on top of 0.5 per staff job.

importFromTier.doc: Auto-import (the buyUtilities order) works from this tier: Village (§3.5).

winterPower.doc: Power demand factor while the Cosy Winter event runs (§5.16).

fundEffect.doc: Coverage effect by funding Low, Normal, High (§5.4).

fundUpkeep.doc: Upkeep factor by funding Low, Normal, High.

pollKeep.doc: Pollution spread: share kept in the cell per pass (gain stays 1 with 4×spread).

pollSpread.doc: Pollution spread: share to each orthogonal neighbour per pass.

pollLag.doc: Pollution moves this share toward its target a month.

roadPollution.doc: Road pollution per unit of load.

industryEmissions.doc: Industry tile emissions for L1–L5 (L5 clean).

lvRateCap.doc: Land value moves at most this much a month (§5.7).

natureTree.doc: Nature coverage per tree tile within natureReach cells, linear falloff (§5.4).

natureWater.doc: Nature coverage per water tile within natureReach cells.

naturePark.doc: Nature coverage per park tile within natureReach cells.

natureReach.doc: Reach of the tree, water and park nature terms; weight 1 − d/(reach + 1).

cultureVenue.doc: Culture coverage per culture point a month of a venue, inside its radius (WP2a choice: the spec gives venues culture rates, not strengths).

cultureRadius.doc: Coverage radius of a culture venue whose catalogue radius is 0 (Museum, Theatre).

cultureFromStock.doc: Every cell gets this share of the town Culture index 100·CS/(CS + cultureHalf) as culture coverage.

healthPerBed.doc: Residents per health bed of need (§5.4: N/250 + N_R/150); capacities are people/this.

healthPerBedRetired.doc: Retirees per health bed of need.

unpoweredEffect.doc: Coverage effect of an unpowered civic building (§5.4).

noRoadEffect.doc: Coverage effect of a civic building with no road within reach (§5.4).

noiseRoad.doc: Road noise per unit of load (§5.4).

noiseIndustry.doc: Noise of an Industry tile of L3 or above.

noiseLeisure.doc: Noise of a Leisure tile of L3 or above.

noiseRail.doc: Noise of a rail track tile.

noiseNightMarket.doc: Night Market: extra noise in cells with Shops (§6.7).

noisePasses.doc: Noise spread passes (same kernel as pollution).

carFreeNoise.doc: Car-Free Centre: noise factor inside the painted area (§6.7: −40%).

cleanAir.doc: Clean Air Rules: industry emissions factor (§6.7: −30%).

psTau.doc: Town pollution stock PS ← S(PS, population-weighted pollution, τ) (§5.4).

visitorWeight.doc: A visitor counts this many residents in CustAccess.

freightScore.doc: FreightScore terms: County Road, rail link + yard, harbour, river barge, Flatland, then the cap (§5.4).

cleanBeachPollution.doc: A beach tile is clean below this pollution (beach appeal +2 per clean tile, §6.5).

densityRef.doc: Residents plus jobs in a cell that count as density 1 (four L5 tower tiles).

youth.doc: Youth Club: crime pressure × (1 − this) within its radius (§6.5).

weights.doc: LV* weights: JobsAccess, Nature, School, Health, Culture, Transit coverage (§5.7).

scenic.doc: Scenic: beach, waterside, hill-top, forest edge (the largest that applies).

premium.doc: Premium = clamp(slope·(mean(Schools, Safety, Health, Fun) − 50) − tax·(HomesTax% − ref), ±cap) (Oates).

potholes.doc: Land value lost on road cells while roads are funded Low (§3.4).

intraMinutes.doc: Travel time of a trip inside one district.

terminalMinutes.doc: Door-to-port time added to every trip between districts.

bpr.doc: BPR factor 1 + alpha·(Load/Cap)^4 with Load/Cap capped (§5.9).

passes.doc: Assignment passes inside a month (successive averages). One pass fits the 3 ms budget; the month-to-month average below supplies the second.

routeBand.doc: Drivers keep their routes until a district's congestion has moved by this share since they last re-routed (stored in lag.routes); times always use the exact factors.

carry.doc: Weight of last month's Load/Cap in the stored congestion: successive averages across months, so a road's BPR settles instead of flipping.

potholes.doc: Travel time factor on roads while roads are funded Low.

carFree.doc: Car-Free Centre: car time factor inside the painted area.

bus.doc: Bus share 0.35·BusCov/100 on covered pairs, at 1.2× car time + 5 minutes.

rail.doc: Rail share 0.40·StationCov/100 on covered pairs; 4-minute wait.

freeBusFridays.doc: Free Bus Fridays policy: bus share factor (§6.7).

maxTransitShare.doc: Bus plus rail share never exceeds this.

peakShare.doc: Share of commuters on the road in the peak (Load is trips per peak).

salesTaxRentShare.doc: Review amendment (§5.17, §18 row 22: 'bases that bite in affordability'): the Tax star feels sales tax as homes tax, scaled by what a household spends in shops and on leisure (α_h + β_h) against this share of income that goes on rent, and measured from the default sales tax so the default calibration is unchanged. Without it 10% sales tax was free money for any town without a linked neighbour to shop in.

taxSlope.doc: Tax star slope per point of homes tax above 3%.

funVenue.doc: Fun star + this when a town-wide venue (Cinema, Stadium) exists (§5.6).

heritage.doc: Culture inflow per heritage tile (level ≥ 2, aged ≥ [1] months), ×[2] under Heritage Protection (§5.6).

diversity.doc: Culture inflow per unit of tier Diversity 1 − Σ share² (§5.6).

needMet.doc: A ladder item met for fewer than this share of a tier's residents counts as unmet (A10).

overcrowding.doc: U_happy − this × the squeezed share of the cohort's tier (§5.15).

overqualified.doc: U_happy − this × the underemployed share of the tier's workforce (§5.15).

irritation.doc: Families and Retirees lose min([1], [0]·(VisitorRatio − tourism.irritationAt)) happiness points (§5.10).

kidStep.doc: Children's tax dials step this much.

adultStep.doc: Adults' tax dials step this much.

loanMultiple.doc: Town Loan up to this many months of revenue.

debtCapYears.doc: Total debt ≤ this many years of revenue.

dsrStop.doc: No new borrowing at or above this debt-service ratio.

civicUpkeepScale.doc: Scales every civic upkeep (A14 calibration; Lab round 1: 0.85, which gives a growing Town the ~10% surplus of §5.13's table).

helperWriteOffDays.doc: Kingsport writes off a Helper Mode advance after this many days (A16).

writeOffBorrowBarDays.doc: No new loan or bond for this many days (24 game months, the rating's memory) after Kingsport writes off an advance, and none at all in Helper Mode. Review amendment: borrowing to the cap and letting the write-off service the debt was a repeatable money machine; A16's guaranteed write-off itself is unchanged.

fundingMult.doc: Civic upkeep × this by funding Low, Normal, High (§5.13).

tripsPerCommuter.doc: Bus or rail fares per transit-riding worker a month (two a working day).

tuition.doc: University fees per resident Student a month (§6.4).

bondSpreads.doc: Bond spread over r_base by rating AAA … B (§5.13).

earlyRepay.doc: Early repayment fee on the principal repaid (§5.13).

ratingDsr.doc: Debt-service ratio below which AAA, AA, A, BBB, BB hold (§5.13).

ratingReserves.doc: Reserves (months of spending) at least this for AAA, AA, A, BBB (§5.13).

ratingHoldMonths.doc: A rating moves one notch once its condition has held this long (§5.13).

ratingOverdraftMonths.doc: Overdrawn for more than this many month ends: rating B (§5.13).

helperMemoryMonths.doc: A Helper Mode episode this recent costs one notch (§5.13).

overdraftLimit.doc: Reserves may go this many months of spending below zero (§5.13).

overdraftTriggerMonths.doc: Helper Mode starts after this many month ends below zero (§5.13).

helperExitMonths.doc: Helper Mode ends when reserves cover this many months of spending (§5.13).

helperEscalateDays.doc: Helper Mode escalation days: services to Low, then the higher tax floors (A16).

helperHomesFloor.doc: Homes tax floor in Helper Mode, and after the second escalation (§5.13, A16).

helperBusinessFloor.doc: Business tax floor in Helper Mode, and after the second escalation.

offerDays.doc: Offers last this many Regional Days (A30).

activeHelloDays.doc: An active mayor sent a hello within this many days (A32).

napHeartbeatMaxDays.doc: Heartbeats stop after this many days without a hello (A40).

initiativeBank.doc: Initiatives bank up to this many.

faces.doc: Mood thresholds of the five faces: grumpy below [0] … beaming from [3] (§5.15).

approvalChecklist.doc: Approval* + this·(100 − perUnmet·#unmet next-tier items) (§5.15 says 0.25; Lab round 1: 0.3, as the founding fortnight's jobless months otherwise hold a hamlet under 50 on day 1; round 2: 0.33, because with the slower meters a plainly played hamlet (the map page's harness bot, the Kid) sat at approval 46–49 for a week with every other Village item met).

approvalPerUnmet.doc: Approval points lost per unmet item of the next tier's checklist.

approvalServices.doc: Approval* + this·(share of the checklists' service-coverage items, green, surgery, police, fire and buses, up to the next tier that hold) (decision 8b: a town that keeps its services covered gets a small approval bonus).

approvalTaxFree.doc: Homes tax up to this costs no approval directly.

talkAt.doc: Town Talk: a star below this is talked about, in proportion to how far (§5.15).

talkTop.doc: Town Talk shows this many items.

wantsMax.doc: At most this many wants bubbles on the map (§5.15).

coveredAt.doc: A home counts as covered by a service where the coverage field reaches this (§7 checklists).

struggleShare.doc: Below this share of its peak population a town shows the struggling badge (§7).

deputyStep.doc: The budget order raises homes tax this much a month (§5.18).

deputyLogKeep.doc: Deputy action cards kept in the inbox.

policyRects.doc: Most rectangles in a painted policy area.

greatMetropolis.doc: The Great Metropolis title: population and Culture star (§7).

poolBase.doc: Tourist pool base (§5.10 says 300; WP2c ×10: at the spec's pool no attraction is ever crowded and no town reaches the 0.6 visitor ratio, so B3 cannot fire).

poolPerPop.doc: Tourist pool per county resident (§5.10 says 0.03; WP2c ×10, see poolBase).

poolPerAttr.doc: Tourist pool per attraction point (§5.10 says 4; WP2c ×10, see poolBase).

stayShopSpend.doc: Shops and leisure spend per stay night.

dayTripSpend.doc: Spend per day trip (60% shops, 40% leisure).

irritationAt.doc: Visitor ratio above which residents get irritated.

season.doc: Real-calendar tourism season, January to December.

coastSwing.doc: Coast sites swing this many times as far from 1.0.

staysPerBed.doc: Stays a bed can host a month (2.5-night stays, §5.10).

maxOccupancy.doc: Most a town's beds are ever filled (§5.10).

baseCap.doc: Visitors a town absorbs with no attractions at all (its green and high street), so crowding is never a division by zero (WP2c choice).

elsewhere.doc: The pull X of resorts outside the county, added to the share's denominator beside 2·mean (WP2c: without it a solo county's share is always 1/3 and reputation does nothing).

gem.doc: Hidden gem: pull ×[0] while population is below the county median and Rep ≥ [1] (§5.10).

quality.doc: Q = ([0] + [1]·Safety/100)·([2] + [3]·Nature/100): smoke and crime hurt tourism (§5.10).

stayShopShare.doc: Share of a stay's £60 a night spent in shops; the rest in leisure (WP2c choice: §5.10 gives the sum only).

dayTripShops.doc: Share of a day trip's spend in shops; the rest in leisure (§5.10).

promotionIrritation.doc: Tourism Promotion's catch: residents' irritation threshold − this (§6.7; review amendment: printed on the card but never applied).

heritageAppeal.doc: Heritage Protection's 'tourism appeal +' (§6.7): appeal per protected heritage tile (built, level ≥ 2, aged as the Culture star's heritage). Review amendment: it was never applied.

ferryFun.doc: Ferry Fun event: coast-site tourist pool ×this (§5.16).

eventDayTrips.doc: Day trips × [0] in a Sunny Weekend and × [1] in a Big Concert (§5.16).

staySat.doc: Stays = pool·share·([0] + [1]·Sat/100), before the beds cap (§5.10).

hotelTaxElasticity.doc: Hotel tax's price term in the tourist pull (§5.13 'also enters the tourist share as a price term'; the §5.10 Share formula omits it): pull × ((1 + default rate)/(1 + HotelTax))^ε from City, so the default 5% leaves the pool calibration as it was and 12% costs about 12% of the pull. Review amendment.

ampBoomBust.doc: Amplitude in a Boom & Bust season.

ar.doc: Noise decay per month in e(m).

noiseMonths.doc: Months of noise summed in e(m).

rSlope.doc: r_base slope per unit of G − 1.

seasonTrend.doc: Within a season, goods fade and offices rise by this much.

seasonMonths.doc: County months per season (6 weeks × 7 days × 12).

tourismLag.doc: World_tourism follows G this many months late.

eventEveryDays.doc: Roughly one World event every this many days.

slowdownAt.doc: Telegraph a slowdown when G will fall below this within 24 months.

fundTrigger.doc: Fund contributions start at this multiple of the median.

awardsPerTownMax.doc: At most this many awards per town per week.

mentionAfterWeeks.doc: A seat without an award gets a Mayor's Mention after this long.

greatWorkTownCap.doc: The quarterback rule: one town supplies at most this share of a stage.

terminalMinutes.doc: Minutes added at each end of a link (§8.2: 5), and a town's own district-to-signpost time until WP2a publishes it. [terminalMinutes]

internalMinutes.doc: Minutes added at each end of a link (§8.2: 5), and a town's own district-to-signpost time until WP2a publishes it. [internalMinutes]

busTime.doc: A bus service makes riders' trips this much shorter (§8.2: "riders −20%"). [busTime]

dayTripLoad.doc: A link's daily trips cap counts a day trip as this share of a day (a month of day trips spread over its days). [dayTripLoad]

closeNoticeDays.doc: Days of notice before a link closes (§8.2). [closeNoticeDays]

commuteDecay.doc: Commuter decay e^(−t/this) and the unemployed's own weight in the denominator (§8.5). [commuteDecay]

commuteStay.doc: Commuter decay e^(−t/this) and the unemployed's own weight in the denominator (§8.5). [commuteStay]

shopDecay.doc: Shopper decay e^(−t/this) and the leak's 0.4 (§5.12). [shopDecay]

shopLeak.doc: Shopper decay e^(−t/this) and the leak's 0.4 (§5.12). [shopLeak]

salesTaxGap.doc: Sales-tax gap: shop appeal × (1 − this per percentage point of gap), clamped (§5.12). [salesTaxGap]

salesTaxGapBand.doc: Sales-tax gap: shop appeal × (1 − this per percentage point of gap), clamped (§5.12). [salesTaxGapBand]

dayTripRate.doc: Day trips DT[j→c] = N_j·rate·AQ_c/(AQ_c + AQ_j + offset)·e^(−t/decay) (§5.10). [dayTripRate]

dayTripOffset.doc: Day trips DT[j→c] = N_j·rate·AQ_c/(AQ_c + AQ_j + offset)·e^(−t/decay) (§5.10). [dayTripOffset]

dayTripDecay.doc: Day trips DT[j→c] = N_j·rate·AQ_c/(AQ_c + AQ_j + offset)·e^(−t/decay) (§5.10). [dayTripDecay]

twinDayTrips.doc: Twin Towns: day trips × this both ways (§8.7). [twinDayTrips]

coachTrips.doc: A coach of day-trippers gift: +this many day trips that month (§6.8). [coachTrips]

shipping.doc: Goods: shipping £ per unit-minute, and the county price's gain and daily step (§8.5). [shipping]

priceGain.doc: Goods: shipping £ per unit-minute, and the county price's gain and daily step (§8.5). [priceGain]

priceStep.doc: Goods: shipping £ per unit-minute, and the county price's gain and daily step (§8.5). [priceStep]

goodsShortfallCap.doc: Goods shortfall cap: a share of the allocation's value (A17). [goodsShortfallCap]

contractShortfallWeeks.doc: Contract shortfall cap: weeks of the contract's value (A17), and Regional Days in a County Week. [contractShortfallWeeks]

weekDays.doc: Contract shortfall cap: weeks of the contract's value (A17), and Regional Days in a County Week. [weekDays]

contractWeeks.doc: Contract length bounds in County Weeks (§8.7). [contractWeeks]

freightPerJob.doc: Freight contracts pay the shipping partner £ per industry job-month (§8.7). [freightPerJob]

sharedDecay.doc: Shared places: e^(−t/this), at most this share of the partner's need, fees per patient- and student-month (§8.5). [sharedDecay]

sharedMaxShare.doc: Shared places: e^(−t/this), at most this share of the partner's need, fees per patient- and student-month (§8.5). [sharedMaxShare]

sharedFees.doc: Shared places: e^(−t/this), at most this share of the partner's need, fees per patient- and student-month (§8.5). [sharedFees]

commuterRule.doc: The commuter rule's transfer per commuter-month, by option (§8.5), and the default option. [commuterRule]

commuterRuleDefault.doc: The commuter rule's transfer per commuter-month, by option (§8.5), and the default option. [commuterRuleDefault]

sharedAir.doc: Shared air (Spirited only): this share of the facing edge's pollution drifts downwind; the Clean Air Pact halves it (§8.5, §8.9). [sharedAir]

housingShare.doc: Player migration: a destination takes at most this share of its vacancies a day; a MoveStory needs this many people (§8.4). [housingShare]

storyMin.doc: Player migration: a destination takes at most this share of its vacancies a day; a MoveStory needs this many people (§8.4). [storyMin]

shieldDays.doc: Community Spirit lasts this many Regional Days (§8.4). [shieldDays]

giftsPerDay.doc: Gifts per sender to each recipient per day; coins as a share of last month's revenue, capped (§6.8). [giftsPerDay]

giftCoinShare.doc: Gifts per sender to each recipient per day; coins as a share of last month's revenue, capped (§6.8). [giftCoinShare]

giftCoinMax.doc: Gifts per sender to each recipient per day; coins as a share of last month's revenue, capped (§6.8). [giftCoinMax]

pranksPerWeek.doc: Pranks per sender to each recipient per County Week (§6.8). [pranksPerWeek]

aidShare.doc: Aid: at most this share of reserves (§8.7). [aidShare]

advertMin.doc: Adverts (§8.6): minimum cost, Regional Days running, awareness, tourist pull bonus, and per-pair weekly limit by rivalry. [advertMin]

advertDays.doc: Adverts (§8.6): minimum cost, Regional Days running, awareness, tourist pull bonus, and per-pair weekly limit by rivalry. [advertDays]

advertAwareness.doc: Adverts (§8.6): minimum cost, Regional Days running, awareness, tourist pull bonus, and per-pair weekly limit by rivalry. [advertAwareness]

advertTourism.doc: Adverts (§8.6): minimum cost, Regional Days running, awareness, tourist pull bonus, and per-pair weekly limit by rivalry. [advertTourism]

friendly.doc: Adverts (§8.6): minimum cost, Regional Days running, awareness, tourist pull bonus, and per-pair weekly limit by rivalry. [advertsPerWeek] (friendly)

spirited.doc: Adverts (§8.6): minimum cost, Regional Days running, awareness, tourist pull bonus, and per-pair weekly limit by rivalry. [advertsPerWeek] (spirited)

stampBuzz.doc: Guestbook stamps: Buzz per distinct visitor per day, capped (§9.10). [stampBuzz]

stampBuzzCap.doc: Guestbook stamps: Buzz per distinct visitor per day, capped (§9.10). [stampBuzzCap]

festivalHost.doc: Festival host: tourist share × (1 + this); linked towns get this share of the extra as day trips (§8.6). [festivalHost]

festivalLinked.doc: Festival host: tourist share × (1 + this); linked towns get this share of the extra as day trips (§8.6). [festivalLinked]

holidayDays.doc: Holiday: at most this many days a season (§2.4). [holidayDays]

seasonWeeks.doc: A season is this many County Weeks (A22). [seasonWeeks]

awardsPerWeek.doc: County Fair: categories drawn each week (§8.9). [awardsPerWeek]

goals.doc: Goals board: goals each week and the rewards' thresholds (§8.7 item 9). [goals]

goalRewards.doc: Goals board: goals each week and the rewards' thresholds (§8.7 item 9). [goalRewards]

festivalWeekendTourism.doc: Festival Weekend: tourist pool × this for a day (§8.7). [festivalWeekendTourism]

twinWeeks.doc: Twin Towns need this many friendship weeks (§8.7). [twinWeeks]

expiryWarnDays.doc: A40: the lobby warns from this many days without a hello; the row is deleted this many days after the heartbeats stop. [expiryWarnDays]

expiryAbandonedDays.doc: A40: the lobby warns from this many days without a hello; the row is deleted this many days after the heartbeats stop. [expiryAbandonedDays]

gazetteFirst.doc: Gazette (§9.9): firsts weigh ×this; last week's leader's score × this. [gazetteFirst]

gazetteLeader.doc: Gazette (§9.9): firsts weigh ×this; last week's leader's score × this. [gazetteLeader]

lateJoinDays.doc: A late joiner (§8.12): a county is "mature" after this many Regional Days; the top-up is this share of the median reserves, at most this. [lateJoinDays]

lateJoinShare.doc: A late joiner (§8.12): a county is "mature" after this many Regional Days; the top-up is this share of the median reserves, at most this. [lateJoinShare]

lateJoinMax.doc: A late joiner (§8.12): a county is "mature" after this many Regional Days; the top-up is this share of the median reserves, at most this. [lateJoinMax]
